intended_object: The docstring and module doc describe the canonical linear map ⨂_i M_i^* → (⨂_i M_i)^* for a finite family of R-modules M_i over a commutative semiring R. It sends ⊗ f_i to the functional ⊗ m_i ↦ ∏ f_i(m_i).
explanation:
The body composes `piTensorHomMap`, which sends ⊗ f_i to `PiTensorProduct.map f : ⨂ M_i → ⨂ R`, with post-composition by `constantBaseRingEquiv`, the isomorphism ⨂_i R ≅ R given by multiplication. The lemma `dualDistrib_apply`, proved just after the definition, confirms the expected formula: `dualDistrib (⨂ₜ f i) (⨂ₜ m i) = ∏ f i (m i)`. The same file also proves that this map is an isomorphism when every M_i is finite free, which is the standard result.

The generality is the natural one:
- Commutative semiring R with arbitrary modules M_i, which is the same setting as the binary `TensorProduct.dualDistrib`.
- `[Finite ι]` is genuinely needed. The product ∏ f_i(m_i) and the isomorphism ⨂_i R ≅ R only make sense for finitely many factors.

This is the n-ary analogue of `TensorProduct.dualDistrib`. Mathlib has no other declaration of this n-ary map, so the counterpart field is left empty.
